name: Container item wire operations
trigger: The player right-clicks a usable bag item or places a carried whole item into another inventory/container slot.
preconditions: The source and destination resolve to valid live container positions; a use has an occupied source slot.
behavior: Uses CMSG_USE_ITEM for the use route; uses CMSG_SWAP_INV_ITEM when both endpoints are in the player's own inventory array; otherwise uses destination-first CMSG_SWAP_ITEM for a bag-to-bag or bag-to-inventory move.
negativeBehavior: Does not send a general swap for two player-array endpoints, does not reverse destination/source byte order, and does not synthesize a local inventory mutation as server truth.

name: Bag-slot click, split, pickup, place, and drag routing
trigger: A bag slot receives left-click, right-click, drag-start, or drag-receive.
preconditions: The window's bag id and the button's physical index resolve to a live slot; modifier state and cursor payload are sampled at the gesture.
behavior: Shift-left on an unlocked stack of at least two opens StackSplit and later calls SplitContainerItem. Ordinary left-click calls PickupContainerItem and repaints. Right-click clears a carried item or calls UseContainerItem. Drag-start and drag-receive both route through the exact left-click path with modifiers ignored.
negativeBehavior: Does not split during a drag, use a locked stack for splitting, preserve an open split dialog after another slot gesture, or treat drag and click as unrelated implementations.

name: Bag-slot tooltip and cursor hover state
trigger: The pointer enters, remains over, or leaves a bag item slot.
preconditions: The slot resolves to an item for a positive hover; merchant, readable, screen-half, and cursor states are available.
behavior: Shows the full item tooltip with left/right anchoring chosen from screen position; selects merchant-sell or readable-inspect cursor where applicable; re-evaluates while hovered; hides tooltip and resets cursor on leave.
negativeBehavior: An empty slot shows no item tooltip; leaving cannot retain a sell/inspect cursor; hover is not frozen if the underlying slot changes.

name: Bag-slot icon, count, lock, cooldown, and button art
trigger: A bag slot is painted or BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN requests a cooldown-only refresh.
preconditions: Container item info and cooldown triple are available for the resolved bag and slot.
behavior: A 37x37 item button paints its icon, bottom-right count only above one, 64x64 quickslot normal ring, depress texture, additive highlight, and centered 36x36 cooldown. Locked items dim to 0.4; empty slots clear icon/count and hide cooldown.
negativeBehavior: Does not display count 0/1, leave a stale cooldown on an empty slot, render a locked item at full intensity, or repaint unrelated state for a cooldown-only event.

name: Physical button to live container-slot mapping
trigger: Backpack or generalized bag slot buttons load and a window repaints.
preconditions: Each button has a physical index; the parent window has a bag id and current capacity.
behavior: Registers left-button click and drag, stores the physical index, maps it through current capacity so the authored bottom-right/up-left chain presents the reference slot order, and hides template buttons beyond live capacity.
negativeBehavior: Does not hard-code a 20-slot capacity into smaller bags, expose out-of-range buttons, or let a capacity change retain stale slot identity.

name: Backpack, equipped-bag, and keyring window rendering
trigger: A container window repaints or its capacity changes.
preconditions: The window has bag id 0, 1..4, or -2 and a current name, capacity, portrait source, and visible slot set.
behavior: Backpack uses the fixed backpack slab and money. Other containers use stitched UI-Bag-Components with row-count and plus-two geometry; equipped bags use their item portrait/name; keyring uses its keyring portrait/title/art variant. Capacity changes refit height and background.
negativeBehavior: Does not show money on non-backpack windows, use backpack art for keyring, retain stale title/portrait, or leave old background geometry after a size change.

name: Container window events, repaint, close, and shown state
trigger: A container frame loads, receives inventory/money/cooldown events, shows, hides, or its close button is clicked.
preconditions: The frame id identifies its container; event arguments identify the changed bag where applicable.
behavior: Registers bag, lock, cooldown, and backpack-money events; scopes full repaints to the affected bag; refreshes cooldowns separately; updates backpack money only; close hides the owning frame; show/hide update the matching bar check state, play container-specific sounds, and relayout the stack.
negativeBehavior: Does not repaint every bag for a scoped bag change, update money on equipped/keyring windows, close a different window, or leave its bar button checked after hiding.

name: Open-all toggle and multi-window stack layout
trigger: The backpack binding/toggle is activated or any participating bag window opens or closes.
preconditions: Backpack plus equipped bag windows 1..4 have current capacities and visibility; keyring is excluded from all-bags membership.
behavior: If any participating bag is open the toggle closes all; otherwise it opens backpack and each equipped non-empty bag. Visible windows stack upward from bottom-right with authored spacing and wrap into a new 192px column when vertical space is exhausted.
negativeBehavior: Does not include keyring in OpenAllBags/CloseAllBags, open empty bag slots, overlap visible bag windows, or keep stale anchors after close.

name: Bag-bar icons, checked state, events, and tooltips
trigger: The bag bar loads, inventory/bag events arrive, a window changes visibility, or the pointer enters/leaves a bag button.
preconditions: Backpack and inventory slots 20..23 resolve; equipped bag item, lock state, binding text, and window visibility are available.
behavior: Maps bar buttons 1..4 to inventory slots 20..23, shows equipped bag icons or empty-bag art, dims locked bags, keeps the corresponding window check state, and shows Backpack with the live OpenAllBags binding or bag-item/Equip Container tooltip.
negativeBehavior: Does not use F1-F4 labels as the live binding, show an equipped icon for an empty slot, retain full brightness while locked, or leave tooltip/cursor state after exit.

name: Equipped-bag bar click and drag placement
trigger: A bag-bar slot is clicked, drag-started, or receives a drag.
preconditions: The button resolves to inventory slot 20..23 and the cursor may be empty or carry an item.
behavior: With an item cursor, PickupInventoryItem equips or places through the paper-doll slot. With an empty cursor, click toggles that equipped bag window. Drag-start and drag-receive both route through the same pickup/place transition.
negativeBehavior: Does not toggle a window while carrying an item, implement drag with a separate semantic path, or target the wrong inventory slot.

name: Level-gated keyring window and button workflow
trigger: The player enters world, bag contents change, clicks the keyring button, or drags a key onto it.
preconditions: Keyring container id -2 is available; level determines capacity; HasKey gates button visibility.
behavior: Computes the level-gated keyring size, shows the button only when the player owns a key, toggles a distinct keyring window, paints keyring art/title, and files a carried key into the first empty keyring slot; a full ring emits the inventory-full error.
negativeBehavior: Does not include keyring in all-bags, show it before HasKey, place into a non-empty slot, silently discard a carried key when full, or use ordinary backpack presentation/sounds.

name: Item-push drop animation on destination bag button
trigger: ITEM_PUSH identifies an item landing in backpack, equipped bag, or keyring.
preconditions: Each destination button owns an animation frame registered for its container id; the pushed item icon resolves.
behavior: Restarts the matching 36x36 icon animation and samples the authored one-second alpha, scale, vertical drop, and horizontal drift keyframes before hiding it.
negativeBehavior: Does not animate the wrong container button, accumulate elapsed time across a restart, continue after one second, or leave stale icon/alpha/position after completion.

name: Game-menu bag-button disable and restore
trigger: The game menu disables bag controls and later restores them.
preconditions: Backpack and four equipped-bag buttons are present with icon and state textures.
behavior: Disables all five controls and greys their icons while preserving button rings; enabling restores input and recomputes each icon's locked/unlocked intensity.
negativeBehavior: Does not let disabled buttons toggle/equip, make the state ring vanish, or force a locked bag back to full brightness when re-enabled.

name: Player aura ordering and discrete lifecycle
trigger: The player aura descriptors or a duration packet change.
preconditions: A player entity and its ordered aura state are available.
behavior: Helpful and harmful auras retain insertion order, repack after removal, update icon/stack/class state from authoritative changes, and cap at sixteen buffs plus eight debuffs.
negativeBehavior: The display does not sort by numeric slot, retain removed entries, mix helpful and harmful indices, or expose hidden client-only auras.

name: Aura countdown permanence and synchronized expiry flash
trigger: A visible player aura is drawn each frame.
preconditions: The aura may have a matching duration packet or may be permanent.
behavior: Timed auras count down from current time and all auras below 31 seconds pulse between 0.3 and 1 alpha on a shared 0.75-second cadence; permanent auras show no timer and never flash.
negativeBehavior: A refreshed duration cannot remain frozen at the old expiry, a permanent aura cannot show zero seconds, and an aura at 31 seconds or above cannot flash.

name: Aura icon stack and debuff-class rendering
trigger: A visible player aura is painted after an authoritative state change.
preconditions: The spell icon and optional dispel class are known.
behavior: Each aura paints a 30-pixel icon, shows a bottom-right stack count only above one, and harmful auras add the authored debuff overlay tinted for magic, curse, disease, poison, or none.
negativeBehavior: Helpful auras cannot receive the debuff overlay, counts zero or one cannot render, and an unknown dispel class cannot escape the default red tint.

name: Player aura hover tooltip
trigger: The pointer enters or leaves a visible aura button.
preconditions: The aura resolves to its player spell metadata.
behavior: Hover presents the aura name, rank, description, stacks, live remaining time, and cancellation guidance, and leaving removes the tooltip.
negativeBehavior: An absent aura cannot retain a tooltip and the remaining-time line cannot be shown for a permanent aura.

name: Right-click aura cancellation
trigger: The player right-clicks a visible player aura.
preconditions: The aura descriptor says whether the helpful aura is cancelable.
behavior: A cancelable helpful aura sends CMSG_CANCEL_AURA with its spell id; harmful and non-cancelable auras are silent no-ops.
negativeBehavior: A debuff cannot address the helpful list or emit a cancel packet, and the packet body cannot contain a slot instead of the spell id.

name: Aura-bar layout and duration typography
trigger: The player aura bar is drawn.
preconditions: One or more helpful or harmful auras are visible.
behavior: MSUI keeps its established top-right anchor, 35-pixel vertical row spacing, compact duration abbreviations and colors, tooltip placement, and stack typography while retaining the same 16-plus-8 capacity and right-to-left rows.
negativeBehavior: The Benilla snapshot's differing anchor, 45-pixel vertical rows, spaced duration abbreviations, warning text color, or tooltip anchor may not overwrite already-functional MSUI presentation without a missing or reproduced-broken finding.

name: Cast and channel lifecycle timing
trigger: The client receives cast start, stop, failure, interruption, delay, channel start, channel update, or channel stop state.
preconditions: The event belongs to the player's active cast or channel and supplies its server timing.
behavior: Casting fills forward, channeling drains backward, delay extends the cast window, channel updates preserve original duration while moving the window, success flashes green then fades, failure holds red for one second then fades, and an expired channel cannot remain stuck.
negativeBehavior: Unrelated failure events cannot replace an active channel, zero remaining channel time cannot remain visible, and frame-rate changes cannot alter the normalized flash/hold/fade windows.

name: Cast-bar geometry status art spark and flash
trigger: A cast-bar phase is visible.
preconditions: Gameplay art and the current cast fraction are available.
behavior: A 195 by 13 status bar uses the authored targeting texture, black half-alpha background, 256 by 64 border and additive success flash, and a 32 by 32 additive spark that tracks the clamped fraction; UIParent-style lower bars adjust its bottom offset.
negativeBehavior: The spark cannot escape the bar, hidden phases cannot draw, and lower action, pet or stance bars cannot overlap the cast bar.

name: Cast-bar label presentation
trigger: A visible cast, channel, failure, or interruption assigns the bar label.
preconditions: MSUI has an established centered cast-label renderer.
behavior: MSUI keeps its existing centered custom cast label and size while updating the text for spell name, Failed, or Interrupted.
negativeBehavior: The Benilla GameFontHighlight declaration cannot overwrite a functional MSUI label merely because its typography differs.

name: Character panel lifecycle tabs and page visibility
trigger: The character panel opens, closes, changes tab, or receives player identity and guild state.
preconditions: The local player and character-page UI state are available.
behavior: The panel initializes hidden, opens the selected page, updates player identity and guild information, preserves tab selection, and closes cleanly with the expected panel lifecycle.
negativeBehavior: Opening one subpage cannot leave another page active, closing cannot retain model input, and an unrelated unit event cannot rewrite the player's character panel.

name: Positive and negative statistic modifiers
trigger: A primary or derived character statistic is formatted with positive or negative modifiers.
preconditions: Base, positive, and negative components are available.
behavior: Positive net modifiers render green, negative net modifiers render red, and unmodified values retain normal text color.
negativeBehavior: A negative modifier cannot be shown as a bonus and an unmodified value cannot inherit stale modifier color.

name: Character statistics resistances and tooltips
trigger: The character paper doll displays or receives a player stat, damage, attack, armor, level, or resistance update.
preconditions: The authoritative player fields and spell-derived modifiers are available.
behavior: MSUI keeps its established broad stat panels, Attack and Ranged labels and values, damage formatting, no-ranged semantics, resistance display, and stat tooltips while updating them from player state.
negativeBehavior: Benilla's alternate panel slicing, labels, weapon-skill substitutions, N/A rules, or formatting cannot overwrite complete MSUI statistics merely because they differ.

name: Equipment slot input state and rendering
trigger: An equipment slot loads, updates, is hovered, clicked, dragged, or receives a carried item.
preconditions: The physical equipment slot, current item, carried payload, modifier state, and lock/broken/fit state are known.
behavior: Slots route the exact equipment container, suppress modifiers where required, support pickup, placement, right-click use, drag and receive, model-pane auto-equip, tooltips, empty-slot guidance, counts, hover/depress art, and locked, broken, or invalid-fit tints.
negativeBehavior: A click cannot use backpack coordinates for equipment, locked items cannot move, modifiers cannot leak into drag routing, and an invalid item cannot be silently equipped.

name: Paper-doll model rotation and carried-item drop
trigger: The player clicks or holds a model rotation button, releases it, or drops a carried equippable item on the model pane.
preconditions: The paper-doll model and current carried item are available.
behavior: MSUI retains its zero default facing and 0.12-radian tap rotation, adds continuous held rotation with start/stop sounds, and auto-equips a valid carried item dropped on the model pane.
negativeBehavior: Rotation cannot continue after release, an invalid carried item cannot equip, and Benilla's different default facing or tap increment cannot overwrite MSUI's established model behavior.

name: Character ammo slot selection and count
trigger: The ammo slot displays, is hovered, or receives a click or drag with ammunition.
preconditions: PLAYER_AMMO_ID, carried item templates, inventory counts, and network session state are available.
behavior: The authored ammo slot shows the selected projectile and total count, accepts only ammunition, and sends CMSG_SET_AMMO with the selected entry; clearing uses entry zero.
negativeBehavior: Non-ammunition cannot be selected, ammo cannot route through equipment swap packets, and displayed counts cannot include unrelated entries.

name: Character-frame authored layout and native MSUI composition
trigger: The character frame and paper-doll page are drawn.
preconditions: The character panel is visible.
behavior: MSUI keeps its complete established paper-doll composition, header, portrait, tabs, model pane, equipment placement, and broad stat backgrounds while retaining the required interactive regions.
negativeBehavior: A structurally different but already-functional MSUI composition cannot be replaced solely to reproduce Benilla coordinates or texture slicing.

name: Item-target enchant confirmation lifecycle
trigger: An armed item-target spell binds an occupied bag or paper-doll item, or the player answers an enchant confirmation.
preconditions: The spell's item-target word is armed; the clicked item and SpellItemEnchantment rows are resolved when available.
behavior: The client applies equipment eligibility, bind-warning, then replacement-warning gates in reference order; Okay can chain into replacement; Yes commits the same CMSG_CAST_SPELL item target; current-target changes hide the questions.
negativeBehavior: Empty clicks, invalid items, Cancel/No, and Escape send nothing and keep item targeting armed; no CMSG_REPLACE_ENCHANT opcode is invented; trade-item replacement is not handled by this packet.

name: Game menu authored composition preserved in MSUI
trigger: Escape opens the in-world game menu.
preconditions: The player is in world and no higher-priority modal owns Escape.
behavior: MSUI keeps its established centered 195x246 dialog, native Video and Interface options, Key Bindings and Macros, while retaining the same dialog art and 144x21 panel-button states.
negativeBehavior: Benilla's 200x288 Era ladder and disabled AddOns, Edit Mode, and Support seats cannot overwrite present functional MSUI choices.

name: Game menu actions and sound kits
trigger: The player opens the menu or clicks Options, Interface, Key Bindings, Macros, or Return to Game.
preconditions: The target page or panel is available and the button is enabled.
behavior: Each live MSUI action opens its existing destination or returns to game and plays the corresponding build-5875 igMainMenu sound kit.
negativeBehavior: Disabled controls cannot fire, and one click cannot stack an unrelated close or bag sound.

name: Server-owned Logout and Exit Game lifecycle
trigger: The player chooses Logout or Exit Game, or a logout response, cancel acknowledgement, or completion arrives.
preconditions: A world session exists for server-backed leave; local quitting intent distinguishes the two identical requests.
behavior: Both actions send empty CMSG_LOGOUT_REQUEST; the exact u32 reason and u8 instant response selects refusal, silent instant completion, or a 20-second CAMP/QUIT countdown; cancel sends CMSG_LOGOUT_CANCEL; completion returns Logout to a refreshed character-select park and exits for Quit.
negativeBehavior: A refusal shows no countdown and disarms quit, early dismissal cannot leave quit armed, expiry cannot manufacture completion, and normal Logout cannot terminate the process.

name: Game menu foreground ownership and lifecycle
trigger: The menu is shown, hidden, or displaced by another menu destination.
preconditions: The in-world HUD and micro/bag controls exist.
behavior: The menu owns input as a modal, the main-menu micro button reflects its pushed state, normal bag interactions are blocked while it is open, and hiding restores gameplay input.
negativeBehavior: Escape cannot open two layers at once, movement and bag actions cannot leak through the modal, and a countdown cannot be re-armed from the menu.

name: Inspect eligibility, request, and target lifecycle
trigger: Inspect is chosen for the current player target, the target changes, or the frame closes.
preconditions: A selectable player unit exists; self, attackable, and targets beyond 10 yards are ineligible.
behavior: NotifyInspect is sent and the 384x512 left panel opens immediately for an eligible target; it follows target changes, closes when the target clears, and uses the exact open/close sounds. The echoed SMSG_INSPECT GUID refreshes data but is not the opening gate.
negativeBehavior: Never inspect self, hostile, non-player, or distant units; never wait for SMSG_INSPECT before opening; never keep stale target data visible.

name: Inspect slot data, refresh, and tooltip behavior
trigger: The paper doll opens, equipment changes, or the pointer enters/clicks an equipment slot.
preconditions: The inspected target remains valid and one of the 19 public equipment slots is addressed.
behavior: All 19 public equipment slots refresh from the inspected unit, occupied slots show their item tooltips, empty slots show their slot-name fallback, and modifier clicks remain inert.
negativeBehavior: Never expose ammo, bag, count, durability/broken tint, or inventory actions through Inspect.

name: Inspect model rotation behavior
trigger: The inspect model opens or either rotation button is tapped or held.
preconditions: The inspected player model is available.
behavior: The full-body model starts at facing 0.61, a tap rotates exactly 0.03 radians in the reference direction, and a held button rotates continuously at 0.5 turns per second with wrapped facing and the rotation sound.
negativeBehavior: Never use character-window zoom behavior, item dressing, or the opposite held-button sign.

name: Inspect equipment slot visual template
trigger: An inspect equipment slot is drawn or hovered.
preconditions: The slot is one of the 19 public equipment positions.
behavior: Each slot uses the 37x37 quick-slot ring, centered icon, square hover highlight, and the reference click/enter/leave/event contract.
negativeBehavior: Never substitute bag-slot round masks, expose draggable inventory behavior, or omit empty-slot hover/tooltip behavior.

name: Inspect frame shell, identity, tab, and model composition
trigger: The InspectFrame becomes visible.
preconditions: An eligible inspected player is selected.
behavior: The 384x512 left-docked frame shows the 60x60 portrait, name, Level race class line, close control, single selected Character tab, four paper-doll quadrants, and the 233x300 model pane at the reference position with paired rotation controls.
negativeBehavior: Never import the omitted Honor tab, title/guild fields, Edit/Dress Up affordances, or replace an equivalent MSUI panel implementation merely for a small structural difference.

name: Inspect equipment slot geometry and frame handlers
trigger: The paper doll and its slot columns are laid out.
preconditions: The InspectFrame is open at its 384x512 reference size.
behavior: Eight left-column slots, eight right-column slots, and the main-hand/off-hand/ranged bottom row occupy the exact reference anchors; the weapon row begins at y=385 client-space, and paper-doll/frame lifecycle handlers remain connected.
negativeBehavior: Never add ammo, relic, or bags; never retain the former raised weapon row or leave model-button handlers disconnected.

name: Mail lifecycle, tabs, refresh and feedback
trigger: Open a real mailbox, enter either tab, receive list/send/failure/close/money events, then leave range or close.
preconditions: In world with a mailbox or a deterministic synthetic panel.
behavior: Open immediately without CMSG_GAMEOBJ_USE, issue throttled list refresh, open backpack, use exact open/tab/close sounds, reset on send success, update purse, and close client-side or beyond five yards.
negativeBehavior: Do not wait for the list reply before showing; do not send CMSG_GAMEOBJ_USE; do not emit duplicate or unrelated sounds.

name: Inbox paging, row state and opening behavior
trigger: Populate inbox with unread/read/COD/item/expired rows, page both directions, hover and open rows.
preconditions: Mail list decoded with more than seven representative rows.
behavior: Filter expired mail, show seven rows per page, clamp arrows/page label, resolve sender and item data, show read/unread colors, COD, expiry and tooltips, then open the selected row.
negativeBehavior: Do not display expired rows, exceed seven rows, lose selection identity, or treat unread and read rows identically.

name: Open-letter read, body, reply, delete/return and attachments
trigger: Open ordinary, returned, GM, item, money, COD and permanent-text mail and invoke each eligible action.
preconditions: Selected inbox row exists; body and item data may arrive asynchronously.
behavior: Mark unread mail once, query body once, render stationery/sender/subject, gate reply, choose delete versus return correctly, take item/money with COD confirmation, and create permanent text items.
negativeBehavior: Do not repeat body queries, allow illegal reply/delete, consume COD attachments without confirmation, or conflate return and delete.

name: Compose validation, money/COD modes and send acknowledgements
trigger: Compose mail with missing/valid fields, body, attachment, send-money/COD values and server acknowledgements.
preconditions: Mail panel open on Send Mail tab with player purse available.
behavior: Require recipient and subject, limit body to 500 characters, charge 30 copper postage, cap COD at 10000 gold, forbid COD without an item and money beyond purse, confirm enclosed money, block while pending, and reset on success.
negativeBehavior: Do not enable invalid sends, send both money and COD, exceed limits, double-send, or retain stale fields after success.

name: Inbox row template and 384x512 shell composition
trigger: Render the inbox tab with representative row states and both page controls.
preconditions: Mail panel visible at gameplay scale.
behavior: Compose the 384x512 four-piece shell, portrait/title, seven 280x50 anchored row templates, icons/borders/COD/count/expiry labels, and exact previous/next button art and anchors.
negativeBehavior: Do not replace a present MSUI-wide placement policy; do not use square bag-style icon framing or alter the seven-row geometry.

name: Compose stationery, inputs and inert scrollbar composition
trigger: Render Send Mail at empty and populated states.
preconditions: Send Mail tab visible.
behavior: Render stationery halves, exact cropped two-piece scrollbar with disabled caps and top knob, recipient/subject/body fields, horizontal divider, cost display, error coin and 500-character body behavior.
negativeBehavior: Do not claim live scrolling or recipient autocomplete; those are explicit Benilla omissions and remain omitted.

name: Compose attachment, money fields, radio controls and frame lifecycle
trigger: Attach/detach an item, edit gold/silver/copper, switch send-money/COD, send/cancel, close and switch tabs.
preconditions: Send Mail tab visible with player inventory and purse.
behavior: Render cropped slot plate and attachment, three money inputs/icons, radio pair, purse, send/cancel controls, close button and two tabs; preserve stated lifecycle and focus gates.
negativeBehavior: Do not add stationery picker, cursor-money drop, recipient autocomplete, or popup-embedded money frames absent from Benilla.

name: Adjacent open-letter frame and action geometry
trigger: Open representative mail and render body, attachment controls and reply/delete/cancel/close states.
preconditions: Inbox visible with an opened row.
behavior: Place a second 384x512 frame adjacent at x=374, render stationery/body/sender/subject/divider, exact cropped scrollbar, letter/item/money slots, and bottom action controls with correct enabled labels.
negativeBehavior: Do not overlay the reader on the inbox, invent auction invoice UI, or claim live body scrolling; those are named source omissions.

name: MultiBars shared runtime and binding contract
trigger: Press or release a bound bottom multi-action key, or interact with a bottom multi-action slot.
preconditions: The player is in world; action slots 48..71 may be populated or empty.
behavior: MSUI keeps both 12-button bottom bars active, maps Benilla wire slots exactly, uses actions on key release, supports mouse use and drag/drop, renders complete action feedback, and shows empty drop wells only while an action payload is held.
negativeBehavior: CMSG_SET_ACTION_BAR_TOGGLES does not hide these bars; an empty slot is not drawn as a permanent visible well; key-down alone does not activate the action.

name: Bottom-left MultiBar composition and twelve-slot mapping
trigger: Enter world with or without actions assigned to BenillaMultiBarBottomLeft.
preconditions: Main action bar is visible.
behavior: A 500x38 high-strata bottom-left host is anchored 17 pixels above the main bar and exposes twelve 36x36 buttons at 42-pixel pitch mapped to action slots 60..71.
negativeBehavior: The host is not conditional on populated actions, does not use the wrong base slot, and remains above overlapping bag panels.

name: Bottom-right MultiBar composition and twelve-slot mapping
trigger: Enter world with or without actions assigned to BenillaMultiBarBottomRight.
preconditions: The bottom-left multi-action host is present.
behavior: A 500x38 high-strata bottom-right host begins 10 pixels after the left host and exposes twelve 36x36 buttons at 42-pixel pitch mapped to action slots 48..59.
negativeBehavior: The host is not conditional on populated actions, does not use the wrong base slot, and does not replace MSUI's already-present vertical multi bars.

name: Party invite popup and exact dismissal wire law
trigger: Receive SMSG_GROUP_INVITE while in world.
preconditions: The invitation carries an inviter name; the player may be alive or dead.
behavior: MSUI plays igPlayerInvite, shows the named invitation for 60 seconds, accepts with one empty CMSG_GROUP_ACCEPT, deliberately sends two empty CMSG_GROUP_DECLINE packets for the Decline button, and sends one decline on escape or timeout.
negativeBehavior: A server cancellation clears without another packet; Accept guards the hide path; the popup never auto-accepts.

name: Party member state, interaction, and lifecycle behavior
trigger: A roster or party-member-stat update changes party1..party4, or the player interacts with a member frame.
preconditions: The roster contains up to four other party members and may have live entity or out-of-range stats.
behavior: Each visible member updates name, health, power type/color, leader/master, connected/dead/ghost/low-health portrait, faction/FFA PvP icon, tooltip, left-click target, and right-click PARTY-menu route; unrelated unit updates do not alter it.
negativeBehavior: Absent members hide; offline forces a full grey health bar and disconnect treatment; power with zero maximum hides; low-health pulse excludes dead/offline/zero-health states.

name: Party member template geometry, art, and layering
trigger: Render any existing party member.
preconditions: The gameplay HUD is visible at the configured MSUI gameplay scale.
behavior: MSUI uses the 128x53 LOW-strata member surface, 37px portrait, exact 70x8 bar offsets, authored UI-PartyFrame overlay, name and leader/master/PvP/disconnect placements, and the six hover/click/update behaviors.
negativeBehavior: The bar fills do not paint over the authored rails, party frames do not draw through MEDIUM panels, and hidden icons remain absent.

name: Four-member cascade and invite event driver
trigger: The party roster gains members or the pending-invite state changes.
preconditions: UIParent and the gameplay HUD are active.
behavior: PartyMemberFrame1 begins at 10,-128 and frames 2..4 cascade at the reference petless 63px stride; the hidden driver maps invite request/cancel state to popup show/hide.
negativeBehavior: No fifth party member frame is created and the deferred pet-frame anchor is not approximated before its own packet.

name: Pet action packed state, input, and wire contract
trigger: SMSG_PET_SPELLS or SMSG_PET_MODE arrives, or the player clicks, right-clicks, shift-clicks, drags, or drops a pet action
preconditions: A controlled unit has a server-authored ten-word pet action bar
behavior: MSUI decodes the exact action/type/autocast/state bits, owns immediate lit/autocast state, sends exact action, stop-attack, and one/two-entry set-action bodies, and enforces pet-only cursor rearrangement
negativeBehavior: Possession blocks rearrangement; unusable unit or disabled-bar state blocks action use; non-pet payloads never populate the bar; refused/passive/self drops do not emit guessed writes

name: Pet token icons, wells, autocast overlay, cooldown, and sparkle
trigger: A pet action slot is rendered or its autocast/cooldown state changes
preconditions: The slot has a command, reaction, spell, blank word, or pet cursor payload
behavior: MSUI resolves the exact command/reaction assets, quickslot state, 58px autocast overlay, 33px cooldown, and four-by-eight GlowStar lap/ramp
negativeBehavior: Blank wells remain hidden without the pet cursor grid; non-autocastable spells never toggle or sparkle; unusable state greys without treating possession as unusable

name: PetActionBar authored frame and ten-button geometry
trigger: The controlled-unit pet bar is shown or UIParent-managed bottom stack changes
preconditions: Gameplay UI is visible; bottom-left multibar may be present or absent
behavior: MSUI draws the 509x43 two-slice shelf, 30x30 buttons from x36 with exact 38px pitch and the unique 37px middle step, at managed bottom 97 or 140
negativeBehavior: The bar does not remain at base height over a shown bottom multibar and does not assume slot classes by position

name: PetActionBar shipped surface ownership
trigger: The PetActionBar UI file surface is compared against the MSUI gameplay draw path
preconditions: The clinical packet includes the complete hash-pinned PetActionBar.xml file fact
behavior: The MSUI bar consumes all ten server words and drives the reference lifecycle, visuals, input, state, and managed layout while retaining the separate existing MSUI pet portrait
negativeBehavior: No small present MSUI difference outside the bar contract is automatically overwritten

name: Quest giver lifecycle and protocol transitions
trigger: A quest-giver list, details, request-items, offer-reward, item-update, or completion packet is applied, or the player invokes a panel action.
preconditions: A valid quest-giver GUID and the applicable decoded quest payload exist.
behavior: MSUI selects exactly one greeting/detail/progress/reward state, clears stale competing states, issues the exact accept/complete/request/choose packet for the clicked action, refreshes item data in place, and closes on completion.
negativeBehavior: Decline and close do not transmit quest packets; progress Continue never requests reward; a reward with choices cannot complete before one choice is selected.

name: Quest giver shared templates and outer frame
trigger: Any quest-giver panel becomes visible.
preconditions: One quest-giver panel state is active.
behavior: MSUI renders the 384 by 512 greeting parchment chrome with the 60 by 60 NPC portrait, centered NPC name, exact close control, shared item rows, coin display, buttons, and scrolling laws.
negativeBehavior: The NPC window does not reuse the Quest Log book icon or overwrite the existing MSUI Quest Log implementation.

name: Quest greeting panel
trigger: SMSG_QUESTGIVER_QUEST_LIST is applied.
preconditions: The list contains greeting text and zero or more quests, and the player quest log is available.
behavior: MSUI splits active and available quests, caps the combined title list at ten, uses selectable title rows with list-select sound, exact scroll viewport, and the exact Goodbye action.
negativeBehavior: A selected title does not leave stale greeting content above details, and Goodbye sends no quest packet.

name: Quest detail panel
trigger: SMSG_QUESTGIVER_QUEST_DETAILS is applied.
preconditions: Decoded title, description, objectives, rewards, money, and giver GUID are available.
behavior: MSUI renders title, body, objectives, choice and fixed reward grids and money in the exact detail scroll panel, plays one WriteQuest sound in instant-text mode, and exposes Accept and Decline at the exact coordinates.
negativeBehavior: Detail reward rows are not selectable, Decline transmits no packet, and stale greeting/progress/reward state cannot mask the detail panel.

name: Quest progress panel
trigger: SMSG_QUESTGIVER_REQUEST_ITEMS is applied.
preconditions: Decoded progress text, required items, required money, completable state, and giver GUID are available.
behavior: MSUI renders the required-money and two-column required-item grid, gates Continue by completable state, and Continue sends CMSG_QUESTGIVER_COMPLETE_QUEST.
negativeBehavior: Continue is disabled when incomplete, never sends REQUEST_REWARD, and Goodbye sends no quest packet.

name: Quest reward selection and completion panel
trigger: SMSG_QUESTGIVER_OFFER_REWARD is applied and the player selects a choice or Complete Quest.
preconditions: Decoded reward text, choice rewards, fixed rewards, money, and giver GUID are available.
behavior: MSUI renders exact two-column choice and fixed reward grids, moves the additive highlight only to the selected choice, gates completion until selection when choices exist, and sends the chosen zero-based reward index on Complete Quest.
negativeBehavior: Clicking a choice does not immediately transmit completion, fixed rewards are never selectable, and Cancel sends no quest packet.
